Resolves #18862

🌿 *Three callers assembled the same selection by hand out of facts the field already owned — after this, selecting a field's text is something the field can be asked to do rather than something its callers must construct.*

A grid cell editor opened with the caret at the end and nothing selected, so typing appended instead of replacing. The fix is one call from the plugin's activation path; the shape of it is the part worth reviewing.

Evidence: L2 (component and e2e tiers, real pointer and keys, plus a browser measurement of what `input[type=number]` supports) → L2 required (every AC is a DOM-observable behaviour). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here (Brain-only — `npm run agent-preflight` reports `Missing script` in this repo); the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: `capability` (`feat`) — `form.field.Text#selectText()` is reusable and separately testable, and §3.1 gives capability precedence even when a bug motivated the work.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `component/grid/CellEditing.spec.mjs` › *grid cell editing — activation selects the value*, three arms — double-click, Enter, F2 — each asserting `{start: 0, end: value.length}` **and** that typing replaces. Red first: 3/3 fail against `dev`'s source with the arms in place |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `e2e/grid/CellEditingExample.spec.mjs` › *number: activation selects the whole value…* on the example's `randomNumber` column (`NumberField`). The component fixture has no editable number column, so the arm lives where its subject exists |
| AC-3 | **Covered by construction, with no arm — deliberately.** The call sits inside the `mounted`-once listener of a newly created editor. The focus-return branch (`startEdit`, the `session?.recordId === recordId && session.dataField === dataField` guard) returns *above* that listener, so a returning focus never reaches it. An e2e arm here would be vacuous: if a second activation gesture failed to reach the plugin at all, the caret would also be unchanged, so the arm would pass without witnessing anything. `onF2Key`'s `!isEditorEvent(data)` filter makes that the likely outcome. I would rather declare the bound than ship a green arm that proves nothing |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The capability lands in the field, not the plugin.** The ticket's Fix says *"select the editor input's full text"* from `grid.plugin.CellEditing`. Doing that literally makes the plugin the **third** site assembling the same main-thread call by hand, after `form/field/trigger/CopyToClipboard.mjs:96` and `plugin/PrefixField.mjs:222` — and the input element id, the range and the `windowId` all belong to the field. So `form.field.Text#selectText()` owns *how*, and the plugin keeps *when*, which is genuinely its (AC-3 is exactly that distinction). Proposed on the ticket before implementing; ACs unchanged.
- **A defect this PR introduced, caught by an existing arm.** `setSelectionRange()` **throws** on an input whose type has no selection API, so the first version of the number arm failed on `The input element's type ('number') does not support selection.` — surfaced by the spec's `pageErrors` gate, not by my assertion. `DomAccess.selectNode()` now makes the range call conditional on `selectionStart !== null`, which also stops the two existing callers throwing there.
- **What a number input can actually do**, measured in Chromium rather than reasoned: `select()` selects the value and `document.getSelection()` reads it, while `selectionStart` is `null` and `setSelectionRange()` throws. So AC-2's behaviour is reachable, but its obvious assertion is not — the arm reads the document selection and then the only thing that matters, that typing replaced.
- **Six existing arms had encoded the defect.** They typed an appended string (`' edited'`, `' draft'`, `' moved'`, `' left'`) and asserted the concatenation. Their subjects are commit terminals, pooling and draft survival — not the caret — so they now type a whole value and assert it, which leaves them insensitive to the activation contract **in both directions** rather than trading one coupling for another. An earlier attempt to preserve their append semantics with an explicit `End` press failed, and the reason is worth recording: `selectText()` is a second async dispatch that lands *after* `editingIn()` reports focus, so it clobbered the keypress.
- **`CellEditingExample`'s `retype` helper** said its select-all handled *"wherever activation left the caret"* — a workaround for this defect, sitting in the suite. Its docblock now says what it is for.

**Not widened:** `CopyToClipboard` and `PrefixField` keep their hand-rolled calls. Converting them is behaviour-preserving cleanup with its own risk surface (`CopyToClipboard` may select a node other than the input), and folding it in turns a leaf into a refactor. It is available now that the method exists.

**Noted, not decided:** `selectText()` dispatches bare, exactly as `component.Base#focus()` does one line above its call site. That makes it new population for neomjs/neo Discussion 18012 (*who owns the terminal outcome of a fire-and-forget `Neo.main` dispatch*), whose four options are all open. Matching the sibling is the consistent choice; adding a terminal here would settle that question unilaterally from a leaf ticket.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-18T13:00:22Z

## Merge-order collision with #18875 — recorded here so it cannot be lost

#18875 (Resolves #18843, @neo-opus-ada, approved) adds `test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingStoreActivity.spec.mjs`. Its `editWithDraft` helper types `' draft'` at `:48`, and five assertions expect the concatenation `'r3c3 draft'` — `:74`, `:86`, `:90`, `:105`, `:113`.

**This PR makes activation select the editor's whole value**, so that keystroke will replace rather than append and the input will read `' draft'`.

Both PRs are green on their own branches, because each is tested against a `dev` that lacks the other. **Whichever merges second turns the other red**, and no CI run on either branch can see it.

This is not a defect in #18875 — its arms are correct against current `dev`, and pre-adapting them would make them red until this merges. The burden sits here, because this is the PR changing the contract:

- **If #18875 merges first:** I update that spec in this PR before handing it off. `editWithDraft` is the single place the draft is typed, so it is one line plus five strings.
- **If this merges first:** #18875 needs the same one line and five strings, and I have said so on its review rather than leaving it to a red run.

The same shape is why this PR touches six existing arms: they had encoded the old behaviour by typing an appended string and asserting the concatenation. `CellEditingStoreActivity.spec.mjs` is simply the seventh, written while this was in flight.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking): `focus()` and `selectText()` are two separate main-thread messages. A keystroke queued between the two tasks lands in the input before the selection does, and is then part of what the next keystroke replaces. Your `End` experiment hit the same seam from the test side. The window is one task wide, so for people it is theoretical, but one main-thread call that focuses and then selects would close it. If a fast-typing report ever shows up, this is where to look.
- **Documented search:** I actively looked for three things and found no concerns:
  - **`selectText()` with no range collapsing the selection.** `setSelectionRange(0, undefined)` would collapse it, but `selectNode()` substitutes 99999 for a missing `end`, which the browser clamps to the value length.
  - **A focus return re-selecting.** The same-session branch in `startEdit` returns before the listener is attached, so the caret a user placed stays theirs.
  - **Editors without text.** `selectText?.()` skips fields that do not extend `Text`, such as a CheckBox editor, and the comment says so.
